sanskrit: suniviṣṭaṃ hitaṃ vākyam uktavantaṃ vibhīṣaṇam abravīt paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ
english: To Vibhīṣaṇa, who had spoken words firmly grounded and well-meaning, Rāvaṇa — urged on by fate — spoke harsh words in return.

sanskrit: vaset saha sapatnena kruddhenāśīviṣeṇa vā na tu mitrapravādena saṃvasec chatrusevinā
english: One might dwell with a rival, or even with an enraged venomous serpent, but one should never live with a pretended friend who serves the enemy.

sanskrit: jānāmi śīlaṃ jñātīnāṃ sarvalokeṣu rākṣasa hṛṣyanti vyasaneṣv ete jñātīnāṃ jñātayaḥ sadā
english: I know the nature of kinsmen in all the worlds, O Rākṣasa — kinsmen always rejoice in the misfortunes of their own kin.

sanskrit: pradhānaṃ sādhakaṃ vaidyaṃ dharmaśīlaṃ ca rākṣasa jñātayo hy avamanyante śūraṃ paribhavanti ca
english: Those who are eminent, capable, skilled, or virtuous in conduct, O Rākṣasa — kinsmen despise them and treat even the brave with contempt.

sanskrit: nityam anyonyasaṃhṛṣṭā vyasaneṣv ātatāyinaḥ pracchannahṛdayā ghorā jñātayas tu bhayāvahāḥ
english: Forever rejoicing in one another's afflictions, perpetrators of harm, concealing their hearts — kinsmen are terrible and cause fear.

sanskrit: śrūyante hastibhir gītāḥ ślokāḥ padmavane kva cit pāśahastān narān dṛṣṭvā śṛṇu tān gadato mama
english: Certain verses are said to have been sung by elephants somewhere in a lotus-forest, upon seeing men with nooses in their hands — hear them as I recite them.

sanskrit: nāgnir nānyāni śastrāṇi na naḥ pāśā bhayāvahāḥ ghorāḥ svārthaprayuktās tu jñātayo no bhayāvahāḥ
english: Neither fire, nor other weapons, nor nooses are what we fear — but kinsmen, terrible and acting from self-interest, are what truly frighten us.

sanskrit: upāyam ete vakṣyanti grahaṇe nātra saṃśayaḥ kṛtsnād bhayāj jñātibhayaṃ sukaṣṭaṃ viditaṃ ca naḥ
english: They will tell others the means of our capture — of that there is no doubt; it is known to us that, among all fears, fear from kinsmen is the most terrible.

sanskrit: vidyate goṣu saṃpannaṃ vidyate brāhmaṇe damaḥ vidyate strīṣu cāpalyaṃ vidyate jñātito bhayam
english: Abundance is found in cattle, self-restraint in Brāhmaṇas, fickleness in women — and danger is found from one's own kinsmen.

sanskrit: tato neṣṭam idaṃ saumya yad ahaṃ lokasatkṛtaḥ aiśvaryam abhijātaś ca ripūṇāṃ mūrdhni ca sthitaḥ
english: Therefore, O gentle one, what is unwelcome to you is that I am honored in the world, that I am born of noble lineage, and that I stand with my foot on the heads of my enemies.

sanskrit: anyas tv evaṃvidhaṃ brūyād vākyam etan niśācara asmin muhūrte na bhavet tvāṃ tu dhik kulapāṃsanam
english: Were another to speak such words, O night-wanderer, he would not survive this moment — but shame on you, O defiler of your lineage!

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ nyāyavādī vibhīṣaṇaḥ utpapāta gadāpāṇiś caturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ
english: Having been thus spoken to so harshly, Vibhīṣaṇa — the speaker of righteousness — rose up into the air, mace in hand, together with four Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā vākyaṃ jātakrodho vibhīṣaṇaḥ antarikṣagataḥ śrīmān bhrātaraṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: And then Vibhīṣaṇa — glorious, his anger now roused, stationed in the sky — spoke these words to his brother, the lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ bhrātāsi me rājan brūhi māṃ yad yad icchasi idaṃ tu paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ na kṣamāmy anṛtaṃ tava
english: You are my brother, O King — say to me whatever you wish; but these harsh words of yours, untrue as they are, I cannot forgive.

sanskrit: sunītaṃ hitakāmena vākyam uktaṃ daśānana na gṛhṇanty akṛtātmānaḥ kālasya vaśam āgatāḥ
english: The well-reasoned counsel spoken out of goodwill is not heeded by those of unformed souls who have come under the sway of Time, O ten-faced one.

sanskrit: sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājan satataṃ priyavādinaḥ apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
english: Men who always speak pleasant things are easily found, O King; but one who speaks — or is willing to hear — what is unpleasant yet beneficial is rare.

sanskrit: baddhaṃ kālasya pāśena sarvabhūtāpahāriṇā na naśyantam upekṣeyaṃ pradīptaṃ śaraṇaṃ yathā
english: I cannot stand by and watch you perish, bound in the noose of Time that carries off all beings, any more than one could ignore a burning dwelling.

sanskrit: dīptapāvakasaṃkāśaiḥ śitaiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ na tvām icchāmy ahaṃ draṣṭuṃ rāmeṇa nihataṃ śaraiḥ
english: I do not wish to see you struck down by Rāma's arrows — those bright shafts blazing like fire and adorned with golden ornaments.

sanskrit: śūrāś ca balavantaś ca kṛtāstrāś ca raṇājire kālābhipannā sīdanti yathā vālukasetavaḥ
english: Those who are brave, powerful, and skilled in arms on the field of battle — when fate overtakes them, they collapse like bridges of sand.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ sarvathā rakṣa purīṃ cemāṃ sarākṣasām svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi sukhī bhava mayā vinā
english: Protect yourself in every way, and this city along with all the Rākṣasas. Fare you well — I shall depart. Be happy without me.

sanskrit: nivāryamāṇasya mayā hitaiṣiṇā na rocate te vacanaṃ niśācara parītakālā hi gatāyuṣo narā hitaṃ na gṛhṇanti suhṛdbhir īritam
english: When I, acting from goodwill, tried to restrain you, my counsel did not please you, O night-wanderer; for men whose time is run and whose life is spent do not accept benefit though offered by friends.

sanskrit: ity uktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rāvaṇānujaḥ ājagāma muhūrtena yatra rāmaḥ salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Having spoken these harsh words to Rāvaṇa, Rāvaṇa's younger brother came in a short time to where Rāma was, together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ meruśikharākāraṃ dīptām iva śatahradām gaganasthaṃ mahīsthās te dadṛśur vānarādhipāḥ
english: Those lords of monkeys standing on the earth beheld him stationed in the sky — massive as the peak of Meru, blazing like a bolt of lightning.

sanskrit: tam ātmapañcamaṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ vānaraiḥ saha durdharṣaś cintayām āsa buddhimān
english: Seeing him together with four others as a group of five, Sugrīva — the irresistible lord of monkeys — pondered the matter with the other monkeys, being wise.

sanskrit: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu vānarāṃs tān uvāca ha hanūmatpramukhān sarvān idaṃ vacanam uttamam
english: Having reflected for a moment, he spoke this excellent speech to all those monkeys, with Hanūmat foremost among them.

sanskrit: eṣa sarvāyudhopetaś caturbhiḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ rākṣaso 'bhyeti paśyadhvam asmān hantuṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: This Rākṣasa, bearing all weapons, advances with four Rākṣasas — see! He comes to kill us, there is no doubt.

sanskrit: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānarottamāḥ sālān udyamya śailāṃś ca idaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Hearing Sugrīva's words, all those foremost of monkeys, raising sāla trees and boulders, spoke these words.

sanskrit: śīghraṃ vyādiśa no rājan vadhāyaiṣāṃ durātmanām nipatantu hatāś caite dharaṇyām alpajīvitāḥ
english: Quickly direct us, O King, to slay these wicked-souled ones — let these short-lived beings fall dead to the earth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇānām anyonyaṃ sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ uttaraṃ tīram āsādya khastha eva vyatiṣṭhata
english: While they were thus talking among themselves, Vibhīṣaṇa reached the far shore and stood there, still stationed in the sky.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahāprājñaḥ svareṇa mahatā mahān sugrīvaṃ tāṃś ca saṃprekṣya khastha eva vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And Vibhīṣaṇa, greatly wise and great in stature, still stationed in the sky, looked at Sugrīva and those others, and spoke in a mighty voice.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo nāma durvṛtto rākṣaso rākṣaseśvaraḥ tasyāham anujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ
english: There is a Rākṣasa of wicked conduct named Rāvaṇa, lord of Rākṣasas — I am his younger brother, known as Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: tena sītā janasthānād dhṛtā hatvā jaṭāyuṣam ruddhvā ca vivaśā dīnā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā
english: By him Sītā was carried off from Janasthāna, after slaying Jaṭāyu; she is confined, helpless and wretched, closely guarded by Rākṣasī women.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ hetubhir vākyair vividhaiś ca nyadarśayam sādhu niryātyatāṃ sītā rāmāyeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: I remonstrated with him through reasoned arguments and various counsels, again and again: 'Let Sītā be properly restored to Rāma.'

sanskrit: sa ca na pratijagrāha rāvaṇaḥ kālacoditaḥ ucyamāno hitaṃ vākyaṃ viparīta ivauṣadham
english: But he, Rāvaṇa, driven by fate, did not accept the beneficial counsel being offered to him — as though it were a bitter medicine.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ paruṣitas tena dāsavac cāvamānitaḥ tyaktvā putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca rāghavaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: I, having been spoken to harshly by him and humiliated like a slave, abandoning sons and wife, have taken refuge with Rāghava.

sanskrit: sarvalokaśaraṇyāya rāghavāya mahātmane nivedayata māṃ kṣipraṃ vibhīṣaṇam upasthitam
english: Report to the great-souled Rāghava, the refuge of all worlds, that Vibhīṣaṇa stands present before him and seeks shelter, quickly.

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvo laghuvikramaḥ lakṣmaṇasyāgrato rāmaṃ saṃrabdham idam abravīt
english: Having heard these words, Sugrīva of swift valor spoke these agitated words to Rāma in the presence of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasyānujo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇa iti śrutaḥ caturbhiḥ saha rakṣobhir bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: One who is known as Vibhīṣaṇa, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa, together with four Rākṣasas has taken refuge with you, my lord.

sanskrit: rāvaṇena praṇihitaṃ tam avehi vibhīṣaṇam tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye kṣamaṃ kṣamavatāṃ vara
english: Know this Vibhīṣaṇa to be a spy sent by Rāvaṇa — I consider his arrest to be fitting, O best of the forbearing.

sanskrit: rākṣaso jihmayā buddhyā saṃdiṣṭo 'yam upasthitaḥ prahartuṃ māyayā channo viśvaste tvayi rāghava
english: This Rākṣasa, directed by a crooked mind, has presented himself — concealed by illusion — to strike once you trust him, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: badhyatām eṣa tīvreṇa daṇḍena sacivaiḥ saha rāvaṇasya nṛśaṃsasya bhrātā hy eṣa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Let him be seized with severe punishment, along with his counselors — for this is Vibhīṣaṇa, the brother of the cruel Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu taṃ rāmaṃ saṃrabdho vāhinīpatiḥ vākyajño vākyakuśalaṃ tato maunam upāgamat
english: Having spoken thus to Rāma, the agitated commander of the army — himself skilled in speech and knowing the value of words — then fell silent.

sanskrit: sugrīvasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvā rāmo mahābalaḥ samīpasthān uvācedaṃ hanūmatpramukhān harīn
english: Hearing that speech of Sugrīva, Rāma of great might spoke thus to the monkeys nearby, with Hanūmat foremost among them.

sanskrit: yad uktaṃ kapirājena rāvaṇāvarajaṃ prati vākyaṃ hetumad atyarthaṃ bhavadbhir api tac chrutam
english: What the king of monkeys has said regarding the younger brother of Rāvaṇa — those well-reasoned words of great weight — you all have heard them.

sanskrit: suhṛdā hy arthakṛccheṣu yuktaṃ buddhimatā satā samarthenāpi saṃdeṣṭuṃ śāśvatīṃ bhūtim icchatā
english: In difficult situations, it is fitting even for a capable and wise friend of good character who desires lasting well-being to offer counsel.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ paripṛṣṭās te svaṃ svaṃ matam atandritāḥ sopacāraṃ tadā rāmam ūcur hitacikīrṣavaḥ
english: Thus questioned, each of them, without delay, spoke their own opinion to Rāma with due courtesy, each desiring his welfare.

sanskrit: ajñātaṃ nāsti te kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu rāghava ātmānaṃ pūjayan rāma pṛcchasy asmān suhṛttayā
english: Nothing in the three worlds is unknown to you, O Rāghava — honoring us, O Rāma, you ask us out of friendship.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi satyavrataḥ śūro dhārmiko dṛḍhavikramaḥ parīkṣya kārā smṛtimān nisṛṣṭātmā suhṛtsu ca
english: You are true to your vow, heroic, righteous, of firm valor — you act only after examining, you are mindful, and you give yourself fully to your friends.

sanskrit: tasmād ekaikaśas tāvad bruvantu sacivās tava hetuto matisaṃpannāś ca samarthāś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Therefore, let your counselors speak one by one, those endowed with sound judgment and capable, with reasons, time and again.

sanskrit: ity ukte rāghavāyātha matimān aṅgado 'grataḥ vibhīṣaṇaparīkṣārtham uvāca vacanaṃ hariḥ
english: When Rāghava had spoken thus, the wise monkey Aṅgada spoke first, for the purpose of examining Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: śatroḥ sakāśāt saṃprāptaḥ sarvathā śaṅkya eva hi viśvāsayogyaḥ sahasā na kartavyo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: One who has come from the side of the enemy is in every way suspect — Vibhīṣaṇa should not hastily be made worthy of trust.

sanskrit: chādayitvātmabhāvaṃ hi caranti śaṭhabuddhayaḥ praharanti ca randhreṣu so 'narthaḥ sumahān bhavet
english: Those of deceitful mind move about having concealed their true intent, and they strike at moments of vulnerability — that calamity would be very great.

sanskrit: arthānarthau viniścitya vyavasāyaṃ bhajeta ha guṇataḥ saṃgrahaṃ kuryād doṣatas tu visarjayet
english: Having carefully weighed benefit and harm, one should adopt a course of action — accept someone on the strength of virtues, and reject on account of faults.

sanskrit: yadi doṣo mahāṃs tasmiṃs tyajyatām aviśaṅkitam guṇān vāpi bahūñ jñātvā saṃgrahaḥ kriyatāṃ nṛpa
english: If the fault in him is great, let him be cast away without hesitation; or if many virtues are recognized, let acceptance be made, O King.

sanskrit: śarabhas tv atha niścitya sārthaṃ vacanam abravīt kṣipram asmin naravyāghra cāraḥ pratividhīyatām
english: Then Śarabha, having reflected, spoke words full of meaning: 'Quickly, O tiger among men, let a spy be employed concerning him.'

sanskrit: praṇidhāya hi cāreṇa yathāvat sūkṣmabuddhinā parīkṣya ca tataḥ kāryo yathānyāyaṃ parigrahaḥ
english: Having properly set a spy of subtle intelligence, and having examined him thoroughly, then let reception of him be made as is proper.

sanskrit: jāmbavāṃs tv atha saṃprekṣya śāstrabuddhyā vicakṣaṇaḥ vākyaṃ vijñāpayām āsa guṇavad doṣavarjitam
english: Then Jāmbavān, discerning, examining with the intelligence of the śāstras, presented a speech full of virtue and free from fault.

sanskrit: baddhavairāc ca pāpāc ca rākṣasendrād vibhīṣaṇaḥ adeśa kāle saṃprāptaḥ sarvathā śaṅkyatām ayam
english: Vibhīṣaṇa has come from a sworn enemy and an evil lord of Rākṣasas, arriving at an unsuitable time and place — let him be regarded with suspicion in every way.

sanskrit: tato maindas tu saṃprekṣya nayāpanayakovidaḥ vākyaṃ vacanasaṃpanno babhāṣe hetumattaram
english: Then Mainda, skilled in right and wrong policy, eloquent in speech, after deliberation, spoke words even more reasoned.

sanskrit: vacanaṃ nāma tasyaiṣa rāvaṇasya vibhīṣaṇaḥ pṛcchyatāṃ madhureṇāyaṃ śanair naravareśvara
english: This Vibhīṣaṇa is, they say, merely a spokesman for Rāvaṇa — let him be questioned gently and with sweet words, O lord of foremost men.

sanskrit: bhāvam asya tu vijñāya tatas tattvaṃ kariṣyasi yadi dṛṣṭo na duṣṭo vā buddhipūrvaṃ nararṣabha
english: Having learned his intent, you will then act in accordance with the truth — if he is seen to be innocent or guilty, do so with deliberate mind, O bull among men.

sanskrit: atha saṃskārasaṃpanno hanūmān sacivottamaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇam arthavan madhuraṃ laghu
english: Then Hanūmān, foremost of counselors and endowed with refinement, spoke words that were smooth, meaningful, sweet, and concise.

sanskrit: na bhavantaṃ matiśreṣṭhaṃ samarthaṃ vadatāṃ varam atiśāyayituṃ śakto bṛhaspatir api bruvan
english: Even Bṛhaspati himself, were he to speak, would not be able to surpass you — best of minds, most capable, foremost among speakers.

sanskrit: na vādān nāpi saṃgharṣān nādhikyān na ca kāmataḥ vakṣyāmi vacanaṃ rājan yathārthaṃ rāmagauravāt
english: Neither for argument nor contention, neither from pride nor personal desire, will I speak, O King — I will speak truly out of reverence for Rāma.

sanskrit: arthānarthanimittaṃ hi yad uktaṃ sacivais tava tatra doṣaṃ prapaśyāmi kriyā na hy upapadyate
english: In what has been said by your counselors on the grounds of benefit and harm, I see a fault — for the proposed course of action does not follow.

sanskrit: ṛte niyogāt sāmarthyam avaboddhuṃ na śakyate sahasā viniyogo hi doṣavān pratibhāti me
english: Without commission of a task, capability cannot be known — hasty deployment appears to me to be flawed.

sanskrit: cārapraṇihitaṃ yuktaṃ yad uktaṃ sacivais tava arthasyāsaṃbhavāt tatra kāraṇaṃ nopapadyate
english: What your counselors said — that deployment of a spy is fitting — the reason for that does not hold, given that the goal cannot be achieved thereby.

sanskrit: adeśa kāle saṃprāpta ity ayaṃ yad vibhīṣaṇaḥ vivakṣā cātra me 'stīyaṃ tāṃ nibodha yathā mati
english: As for the charge that Vibhīṣaṇa has arrived at an unsuitable time and place — I have something to say about that; hear it as I understand it.

sanskrit: sa eṣa deśaḥ kālaś ca bhavatīha yathā tathā puruṣāt puruṣaṃ prāpya tathā doṣaguṇāv api
english: That very place and time become what they become depending on the person encountered; and so too do virtues and faults, passing from person to person.

sanskrit: daurātmyaṃ rāvaṇe dṛṣṭvā vikramaṃ ca tathā tvayi yuktam āgamanaṃ tasya sadṛśaṃ tasya buddhitaḥ
english: Having seen the wickedness of Rāvaṇa, and likewise your own valor, his coming here is fitting and consistent with his own discernment.

sanskrit: ajñātarūpaiḥ puruṣaiḥ sa rājan pṛcchyatām iti yad uktam atra me prekṣā kā cid asti samīkṣitā
english: Regarding what was said — 'Let him be questioned by men in disguised form' — I have a considered opinion about that, upon reflection.

sanskrit: pṛcchyamāno viśaṅketa sahasā buddhimān vacaḥ tatra mitraṃ praduṣyeta mithyapṛṣṭaṃ sukhāgatam
english: A wise man, when questioned suddenly with suspicion, might speak guardedly — and thereby a friend who came in good faith would be alienated by false questioning.

sanskrit: aśakyaḥ sahasā rājan bhāvo vettuṃ parasya vai antaḥ svabhāvair gītais tair naipuṇyaṃ paśyatā bhṛśam
english: It is not possible, O King, to know another's inner disposition suddenly — rather, it is by those inner traits that are revealed that one skilled in discernment perceives it deeply.

sanskrit: na tv asya bruvato jātu lakṣyate duṣṭabhāvatā prasannaṃ vadanaṃ cāpi tasmān me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: But even as he speaks, no wickedness of disposition is ever discernible in him — his countenance is serene — and therefore I have no doubt.

sanskrit: aśaṅkitamatiḥ svastho na śaṭhaḥ parisarpati na cāsya duṣṭā vāk cāpi tasmān nāstīha saṃśayaḥ
english: One of undisturbed mind, at ease — a deceitful person does not move about in such a manner; his speech too is not crooked — and therefore there is no doubt here.

sanskrit: ākāraś chādyamāno 'pi na śakyo vinigūhitum balād dhi vivṛṇoty eva bhāvam antargataṃ nṛṇām
english: Demeanor, even when one attempts to conceal it, cannot be fully hidden — it forcibly reveals the inner disposition of men.

sanskrit: deśakālopapannaṃ ca kāryaṃ kāryavidāṃ vara saphalaṃ kurute kṣipraṃ prayogeṇābhisaṃhitam
english: An action suited to place and time, O best of those who know what must be done, when undertaken with purposeful application, quickly bears fruit.

sanskrit: udyogaṃ tava saṃprekṣya mithyāvṛttaṃ ca rāvaṇam vālinaś ca vadhaṃ śrutvā sugrīvaṃ cābhiṣecitam
english: Having seen your resolve, having seen Rāvaṇa's false conduct, and having heard of the slaying of Vālin and the consecration of Sugrīva —

sanskrit: rājyaṃ prārthayamānaś ca buddhipūrvam ihāgataḥ etāvat tu puraskṛtya yujyate tv asya saṃgrahaḥ
english: — desiring a kingdom, he has come here with considered intent; keeping all this in view, his acceptance is appropriate.

sanskrit: yathāśakti mayoktaṃ tu rākṣasasyārjavaṃ prati tvaṃ pramāṇaṃ tu śeṣasya śrutvā buddhimatāṃ vara
english: What I have said to the best of my ability regarding the Rākṣasa's sincerity — you are the authority for the rest, O best of the wise, having heard it.

sanskrit: atha rāmaḥ prasannātmā śrutvā vāyusutasya ha pratyabhāṣata durdharṣaḥ śrutavān ātmani sthitaḥ
english: Then Rāma — of serene spirit, irresistible, learned, and established in his own self — having heard the son of the Wind, replied.

sanskrit: mamāpi tu vivakṣāsti kā cit prati vibhīṣaṇam śrutam icchāmi tat sarvaṃ bhavadbhiḥ śreyasi sthitaiḥ
english: I too have something to say regarding Vibhīṣaṇa — I wish to hear all of that from you who stand in what is good.

sanskrit: mitrabhāvena saṃprāptaṃ na tyajeyaṃ kathaṃ cana doṣo yady api tasya syāt satām etad agarhitam
english: One who has come in the spirit of friendship I would not abandon under any circumstances — even if fault there be in him, this is not censured among the good.

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvaḥ plavageśvaraḥ pratyabhāṣata kākutsthaṃ sauhārdenābhicoditaḥ
english: Hearing Rāma's words, Sugrīva — lord of the leaping monkeys — spoke back to the scion of Kākutstha, impelled by warm affection.

sanskrit: kim atra citraṃ dharmajña lokanāthaśikhāmaṇe yat tvam āryaṃ prabhāṣethāḥ sattvavān sapathe sthitaḥ
english: What is remarkable in this, O knower of dharma, O crest-jewel of the lords of the world, that you, possessed of true being and standing on the noble path, should speak what is noble?

sanskrit: mama cāpy antarātmāyaṃ śuddhiṃ vetti vibhīṣaṇam anumanāc ca bhāvāc ca sarvataḥ suparīkṣitaḥ
english: My own inner self too perceives the purity of Vibhīṣaṇa — from inference, from his disposition, he has been thoroughly examined from every angle.

sanskrit: tasmāt kṣipraṃ sahāsmābhis tulyo bhavatu rāghava vibhīṣaṇo mahāprājñaḥ sakhitvaṃ cābhyupaitu naḥ
english: Therefore, O Rāghava, let the greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa quickly become our equal and let him enter into friendship with us.

sanskrit: sa sugrīvasya tad vākyaṃ rāmaḥ śrutvā vimṛśya ca tataḥ śubhataraṃ vākyam uvāca haripuṃgavam
english: Rāma, having heard and reflected upon that speech of Sugrīva, then spoke more auspicious words to the bull among monkeys.

sanskrit: suduṣṭo vāpy aduṣṭo vā kim eṣa rajanīcaraḥ sūkṣmam apy ahitaṃ kartuṃ mamāśaktaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Whether this night-wanderer be utterly wicked or free of wickedness — how could he ever be capable of doing even the slightest harm to me?

sanskrit: piśācān dānavān yakṣān pṛthivyāṃ caiva rākṣasān aṅgulyagreṇa tān hanyām icchan harigaṇeśvara
english: Piśācas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and all the Rākṣasas on earth — I could slay all of them with the tip of my finger, were I so inclined, O lord of the monkey host.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi kapotena śatruḥ śaraṇam āgataḥ arcitaś ca yathānyāyaṃ svaiś ca māṃsair nimantritaḥ
english: It is heard that a dove, when an enemy sought refuge with him, honored the enemy properly and even invited him with portions of his own flesh.

sanskrit: sa hi taṃ pratijagrāha bhāryā hartāram āgatam kapoto vānaraśreṣṭha kiṃ punar madvidho janaḥ
english: That dove accepted even him who had come to carry off his wife — then what of a man of my kind, O best of monkeys?

sanskrit: ṛṣeḥ kaṇvasya putreṇa kaṇḍunā paramarṣiṇā śṛṇu gāthāṃ purā gītāṃ dharmiṣṭhāṃ satyavādinā
english: Hear the verses sung of old by Kaṇḍu, son of the sage Kaṇva, that great sage, righteous and truthful in speech.

sanskrit: baddhāñjalipuṭaṃ dīnaṃ yācantaṃ śaraṇāgatam na hanyād ānṛśaṃsyārtham api śatruṃ paraṃ pata
english: One should not slay a suppliant who stands with palms joined, pitiable, begging for protection, come seeking refuge — even if he be the greatest enemy — for the sake of non-cruelty, O lord of birds.

sanskrit: ārto vā yadi vā dṛptaḥ pareṣāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ariḥ prāṇān parityajya rakṣitavyaḥ kṛtātmanā
english: Whether afflicted or proud, an enemy who has taken refuge with others must be protected by one of formed soul, even at the sacrifice of his own life.

sanskrit: sa ced bhayād vā mohād vā kāmād vāpi na rakṣati svayā śaktyā yathātattvaṃ tat pāpaṃ lokagarhitam
english: If he does not protect — out of fear, or delusion, or desire — to the best of his ability and in accordance with truth, that is a sin censured by the world.

sanskrit: vinaṣṭaḥ paśyatas tasya rakṣiṇaḥ śaraṇāgataḥ ādāya sukṛtaṃ tasya sarvaṃ gacched arakṣitaḥ
english: If the refugee perishes while the protector watches, the refugee — left unprotected — departs taking with him all the merit of that protector.

sanskrit: evaṃ doṣo mahān atra prapannānām arakṣaṇe asvargyaṃ cāyaśasyaṃ ca balavīryavināśanam
english: Such is the great fault in not protecting those who have surrendered — it leads to exclusion from heaven, to disgrace, and to destruction of strength and valor.

sanskrit: kariṣyāmi yathārthaṃ tu kaṇḍor vacanam uttamam dharmiṣṭhaṃ ca yaśasyaṃ ca svargyaṃ syāt tu phalodaye
english: I will fulfill in all truth the excellent teaching of Kaṇḍu — righteous and glorious, it shall yield the fruit of heaven when the time of fruition comes.

sanskrit: sakṛd eva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dadāmy etad vrataṃ mama
english: To one who has surrendered even once and cries 'I am yours' — I grant freedom from fear from all beings: this is my vow.

sanskrit: ānayainaṃ hariśreṣṭha dattam asyābhayaṃ mayā vibhīṣaṇo vā sugrīva yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam
english: Bring him here, O best of monkeys — I have given him my assurance of safety, O Sugrīva, whether it be Vibhīṣaṇa, or even Rāvaṇa himself.

sanskrit: tatas tu sugrīvavaco niśamya tad dharīśvareṇābhihitaṃ nareśvaraḥ vibhīṣaṇenāśu jagāma saṃgamaṃ patatrirājena yathā puraṃdaraḥ
english: Then, upon hearing those words spoken by the lord of men at the urging of the lord of monkeys, the king of men swiftly went to meet Vibhīṣaṇa, as Purandara meets the king of birds.
